name: Margaret Glaser
fact: She sat on the Judicial Council as an Associate Justice in 2022-23, under Chief Justice Justin Goins and Associate Chief Justice Isaac King, alongside Colton Ping, Garrett Baum, Ellie Soares and Miles Huff. The archive records her only as a senator-at-large in 2021-22.

name: Madison Payne
fact: She sat on the Judicial Council as an Associate Justice in 2024-25, under Chief Justice Ellen Henderson and Associate Chief Justice Morgan Gammons, alongside Neill Kane, Aziz Umarov and Sam Dorris. The archive records her only as a member in 2023-24.

name: Justin Goins
fact: He joined the Judicial Council as an Associate Justice in 2021-22, under Chief Justice Holden Schroeder and Associate Chief Justice Turner Reynolds, sitting with Alexis Mayne, Jason Herlick, Abbey Norvell and Nicole Massarone, before becoming Chief Justice the following year.

name: Blake Graham
fact: He was already an Associate Justice before he became Chief Justice, sitting under Chief Justice Morgan Gammons with Associate Chief Justice Gavin Grawe, Neill Kane, Aziz Umarov, Hailey Stapleton and Samantha Lein. The archive records him only as Chief Justice in 2025-26.

name: Tribhuwan Singh

name: Elizabeth DeLozier
fact: After serving as Secretary of the Senate in 2021-22 she sat in the 2022-23 Senate as the College of Health and Human Services senator, where SGA's own roster spells her surname Delozier.

name: Ethan Huffaker
fact: After his year as Secretary of the Senate he read philosophy, won a Faculty-Undergraduate Student Engagement grant to work with Dr Landon Elkind, and on 7-9 June 2024 presented their co-authored paper on the proofs of Principia Mathematica to the Bertrand Russell Society's 51st annual meeting in Amherst, New York. The paper reconstructed 126 complete proofs, running to 137 pages against the 33 pages of proof sketches in the original.

src.label: WKU News, 'WKU Philosophy Student Presents Research at National Philosophy Meeting', 14 June 2024

name: Will Hemenover
fact: A Mahurin Honors College scholar of the class of 2024, double majoring in Biology and Environmental, Sustainability and Geographic Sciences. Alongside the Senate he was an HonorsTopper, twice an H4 first-year orientation counsellor, an ambassador for the Department of Earth, Environmental and Atmospheric Sciences, a member of the disc golf club team, and spent the summer of 2022 as a horticulture intern on WKU's Farm-to-Table Program.

src.label: WKU News, 'Will Hemenover - Scholar Spotlight', 14 October 2022

name: Arivumani Srivastava
fact: He sat as the Gatton Academy senator while still a senior at the Academy. In December 2021 he won a $1,500 Doctors Mody Service Learning grant for the Hardin Planetarium, where he had volunteered since 2019, to rebuild its museum displays; he called it his capstone contribution. He was also legislative coordinator of the Kentucky Student Voice Team, and was cited in an amicus brief to the United States Supreme Court.

src.label: WKU News, 'Gatton Academy student secures grant for Hardin Planetarium', 9 December 2021

name: Annie Finch
fact: She was one of forty-two candidates for WKU's 2024 Homecoming queen, from Louisville, an Elementary Education major, and the Student Government Association was her sponsoring organisation. She was not crowned; Sarah Vincent won, with Jozee Bond and Rosie Ribble the runners-up. As with every one of these candidate announcements, WKU published no portraits of the candidates.

src.label: WKU News, '42 WKU students candidates for 2024 Homecoming queen', 1 November 2024

name: Avery Wells
fact: PHOTOGRAPH LEAD, NOT A CONFIRMED ONE. An Avery Wells of Louisville, son of Andre and Antissa Wells, a Political Science major with an African American Studies minor sponsored by the National Pan-Hellenic Council, was crowned WKU's 2023 Coming Home King on 25 February 2023. The following year's candidate announcement carries the photograph of that crowning under a full positional caption, 'The 2023 Coming Home King was Avery Wells (center); first runner-up was Harrison Snyder (right) and second runner-up was Adan Canizalez (left)', at www.wku.edu/img_news/article_images/11746.jpg, which is downloadable. It is the only positionally-keyed photograph of anyone named Avery Wells in a WKU source. It was not published here because it has the same gap the withdrawal register already records for the Herald frames of him: nothing in any source ties this student to the 2020-21 senate, and the archive's Avery Wells is a 2020-21 member only.

src.label: WKU News, '22 WKU students candidates for 2024 Coming Home King', 6 February 2024

name: Zachary Skillman

They are identical twins, so the archive's confirmed Herald portrait of Jacob cannot separate them either. The frame is unusable for Zachary and should not be re-found.

name: Blake Graham
fact: PHOTOGRAPH ROUTE CLOSED, NOT A NEW LEAD. The previous officer pass could not download wkuherald.com images and left one open question: the frame of 11 November 2025 (SAV2487.jpg) is captioned 'Associate Justice Sophie Stirling (left) and Associate Justice Hannah Hash (right) are introduced by Chief Justice Blake Graham', so if it held exactly three people the third would be Graham by elimination. The Herald served the file this run and it was opened. It does not hold three people: two women sit in the foreground and at least four more sit behind them, a woman at the left edge, two men at the right and a further woman at the right edge. Elimination therefore identifies nobody. The right-hand foreground woman is Hannah Hash, and the archive's existing 2025-26-hannah-hash.jpg is cut from this same photograph, which confirms the caption reads as written. Graham is not identifiable in it. The frame of the same meeting captioned 'gives his final report' (SAV2500.jpg) was also opened and the withdrawal register is exactly right about it: the camera is behind him and he is an out-of-focus back of a head at the right edge, facing a room of seated senators. Both frames stay withdrawn.

src.label: College Heights Herald, 11 November 2025, SGA meeting in the Senate Chambers

name: Zachary Skillman
fact: PHOTOGRAPH ROUTE CLOSED. WKU's own feature on the Skillman brothers of 2 February 2022 says outright, in its own words, that they are 'identical twin brothers from Katy, Texas', both WKU juniors reading Business Economics with minors in Computer Information Systems, both formerly on the Cross Country and Track and Field team, both Gordon Ford College of Business ambassadors and peer tutors, and both serving as Senators at-Large for the Student Government Association. The one photograph shows the two of them side by side outside Grise Hall in matching white WKU polos, the alt attribute is empty and the article carries no left-or-right cue anywhere in its text. The archive's confirmed Herald portrait of Jacob Skillman cannot separate them because the university itself calls them identical. This frame can never identify Zachary and should not be re-found.

name: Tribhuwan Singh
fact: He was also an officer of WKU's Interfraternity Council for 2021, holding the Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Activities portfolio, and was then an Elizabethtown junior and a member of Phi Delta Theta. WKU's announcement of the IFC officers carries a photograph of eight men, but it names nine officers, gives no positions, has an empty alt attribute and no caption, and every man in it is masked, so it identifies nobody and is not a portrait source. The same fraternity chapter listing recurs in WKU's 2022 Greek awards announcement, whose only photograph is of a sorority.

src.label: WKU News, 'Interfraternity Council announces 2021 officers', 26 January 2021

name: Livi Ray
fact: She sat as the Gatton Academy senator and Secretary of the Senate while a Gatton Academy senior of the class of 2024, from University Heights Academy in Hopkinsville. Her research project, 'Dual Partisanship in America: Dead or Alive?', was mentored by Dr Scott Lasley and Dr Joel Turner of the Department of Political Science and was one of the WKU projects presented at Posters-at-the-Capitol in Frankfort. She spent the summer of 2023 as a Congressional intern in Washington through the House of Representatives, and she was one of the two students her class chose to speak at its graduation. No photograph identifies her: WKU's coverage of her illustrates the Capitol trip with an uncaptioned group of seven, the summer story with an unkeyed collage of nineteen faces, and the graduation with the whole class of eighty-nine in caps and gowns.

src.label: WKU News, '89 Gatton Academy Graduates Honored in the Class of 2024'

name: Fatin Yaro
fact: Originally from Burkina Faso, he was a WKU Global Affairs graduate assistant and a doctoral student in education, and he presented 'Friendship & Survival', a reading of the relationships in Toni Morrison's Sula from the perspective of an international student, at the English Department's Global Learning Forum. He graduated in the autumn of 2023. The forum article is illustrated only by the Global Learning Forum logo, and WKU's faculty and staff photograph directory holds no portrait under any NetID of the form fatin_yaro###, all one thousand having been checked.

src.label: WKU News, 'English Department Leads Global Learning Forum Discussion'

name: Justin Goins
fact: REJECTED PHOTOGRAPH LEAD, recorded so it is not re-found as new. WKU's report of the English Department's third annual essay contest, 17 February 2020, records that 'Justin Goins of McCracken County High School won third place' in the Creative Writing Contest, and carries a photograph of three high-school winners holding their certificates with two faculty members. It cannot be used. The identification method that worked for Karley Solorzano, reading the recipient's name off the certificate in the frame, fails here: WKU serves the image at only 500x500 and the name line on the certificate is illegible at any enlargement. The caption is empty, nine winners are named in the text against three students shown, and two of the nine have male given names, Justin Goins and Peter Thiessen, so the one young man in the picture cannot be told between them. It is in any case not established that the McCracken County high-school pupil of February 2020 is the Justin Goins who joined the Judicial Council in 2021-22.

src.label: WKU News, 'WKU English Department Awards Nine Winners for Essay Contest', 17 February 2020

WKU SGA's executive headshots directory at wku.edu/sga/executive/headshots/ still serves files although the directory listing itself is refused, and it holds the 2019-20 and 2020-21 cabinets under given-name filenames: garrett.jpg and garrett_new.jpg, will.jpg, ashlynn.jpg, paul.jpg, matt.jpg and kody.jpg. The year-foldered variants of this path used in later years, 2021-2022-executive, 2022-2023-executive/exec_headshots, 2023-2024-executive/headshots, 2024-2025-executive and 2025_2026_executive/headshots_website, were probed for every senator and justice on this block under given-name, firstname_lastname, firstname_lastname_min and lastname_firstname_headshot forms and returned nothing.
